correctness.rationale: Symmetric PBH says the lost space is the sum of eigenspace intersections with x_0=0. The zero eigenvalue has only constants. For λ=2−2cos θ away from 0 and 4, the two arc solutions are multiples of sin(jθ). If q=x_d is nonzero, neither endpoint sine vanishes; subtracting the endpoint equations gives sin(dθ)+sin(mθ)−sin(nθ)=4sin(nθ/2)sin(dθ/2)sin(mθ/2)=0. The endpoint nonvanishing forces θ=2πk/n even for complex θ, so the two cosecants cancel in the leader equation and force w=0, excluded. With q=0 the leader equation makes the arc amplitudes opposite and the far-end equation makes the two endpoint cosine parities equal. Hence the modes are exactly the cycle sines with 1≤k<n/2 and n dividing 2kd, one per admissible k; their count is the number of positive integers s<g/2, namely floor((g−1)/2). At the repeated root λ=4 the zero-start arc solutions are alternating and linear in distance. For q≠0 the far endpoint requires w=1/d+1/m, and the leader requires w=(−1)^d/d+(−1)^m/m; agreement is exactly the stated even-even parity. For q=0 the repeated-root solutions are zero; otherwise q fixes the entire vector, so the extra dimension is exactly one. The series-arc parallel-resistance calculation gives R=dm/(d+m); w*=1 occurs only at d=m=2. Independent exact ranks over Q matched 469 distinct configurations for n=4–24, all allowable d, using 1, 1/2, 3/2 and, for even-even arcs, w* and w*±1/1000. All 36 resonance vectors and 72 near-resonance ranks were checked. Replay: for each rational w, clear denominators in L, form the n Krylov columns by repeated integer matrix-vector products starting at e_0, and row-reduce over Q. These finite checks support but do not extend the analytic proof to arbitrary real weights by themselves.

value.rationale: One added link and one input at its endpoint are natural minimal changes to a cycle. A full rank law rather than a generic controllability assertion distinguishes persistent arithmetic loss from an isolated tunable loss. It identifies the exact positive weight to avoid, relates it to a network invariant (inverse pre-chord resistance), and proves there is no hidden second resonance. For instance, on the six-cycle with chord 0–2 the controllability verdict itself changes only at w=3/4. This is useful structural information for fixed-weight leader placement without asserting an energy or robustness bound.
